session.question: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
session.answer:
In men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA), elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) was associated with the chromosomal anomaly group, indicating more severe testicular dysfunction in these patients. This pattern was particularly marked in Klinefelter syndrome (KS), which also showed lower testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, higher luteinizing hormone (LH), greater height and arm span, and gynecomastia more frequently than men with an undefined cause of NOA. (riccetto2022clinicalandlaboratory chunk 1)

The testicular XX disorder of sex development (testicular XX DSD) subgroup showed an intermediate endocrine phenotype, with LH, FSH, and penile length values between those of KS and the undefined cause group. Testicular volume in testicular XX DSD was similar to KS, whereas the remaining clinical findings were closer to the undefined cause group. (riccetto2022clinicalandlaboratory chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-6f892952: In this retrospective study of men aged 20–40 with non-obstructive azoospermia, chromosomal anomaly cases (including Klinefelter syndrome, mosaic KS, testicular XX, and other sex chromosome/autosomal anomalies) were compared with cases of undefined cause. Elevated FSH was associated with the chromosomal anomaly group, especially Klinefelter syndrome, which also showed lower testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, higher LH, greater height and arm span, and gynecomastia more often present. The testicular XX DSD subgroup had LH, FSH, and penile length values intermediate between KS and the undefined group, testicular volume similar to KS, and other findings closer to the undefined group.
From Luísa Riccetto, Tarsis Paiva Vieira, Nilma Lucia Viguetti-Campos, Tais Nitsch Mazzola, Mara Sanches Guaragna, Helena Fabbri-Scallet, Maricilda Palandi de Mello, Antonia Paula Marques-de-Faria, Andrea Trevas Maciel-Guerra, and Gil Guerra. Clinical and laboratory differences between chromosomal and undefined causes of non-obstructive azoospermia: a retrospective study. São Paulo Medical Journal, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1590/1516-3180.2022.0281.r1.30082022, doi:10.1590/1516-3180.2022.0281.r1.30082022.

pqac-0b3cec51: The excerpt is about non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and predictors of sperm retrieval after micro-TESE, especially testosterone-to-LH ratio, FSH, and testicular volume. It does not mention chromosomal anomalies, Klinefelter syndrome (KS), testicular XX DSD, or comparisons with an undefined cause group. The relevant findings are that higher serum FSH and LH were associated with failed sperm retrieval, while larger testicular volume and higher T/LH ratio were associated with successful retrieval.
From Tae Jin Kim and Kyo Chul Koo. Testosterone to luteinizing hormone ratio as a potential predictor of sperm retrieval in non-obstructive azoospermia patients. Yonsei Medical Journal, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3349/ymj.2023.0054, doi:10.3349/ymj.2023.0054.

pqac-232f8262: The excerpt describes a retrospective cohort of 10,388 men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and severe oligozoospermia, focusing on when AZF screening is indicated in patients with chromosomal abnormalities. It reports that certain karyotypes, including inv(Y)(p11.2q12), idic(Y)(q11.2), 46,XY,r(Y), idic(Y)(p11.2), and der(Y;Autosome), should be referred for AZF deletion screening. The abstract also notes a secondary analysis correlating sperm count with Y chromosome microdeletions, finding YCMs in only 1% of cases with sperm counts above 1×10^6/mL. No specific information about FSH, Klinefelter syndrome, testicular XX DSD, or comparison to an undefined cause group is provided in this excerpt.
From Hamid Kalantari, Marjan Sabbaghian, Paraskevi Vogiatzi, Amarnath Rambhatla, Ashok Agarwal, Giovanni M. Colpi, and Mohammad Ali Sadighi Gilani. Bridging the gap between azf microdeletions and karyotype: twelve years’ experience of an infertility center. The World Journal of Men's Health, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.5534/wjmh.220089, doi:10.5534/wjmh.220089.
